newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up in slow trading on Thursday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 20,660 yuan ($2,489) per tonne, rising 160 yuan. It opened at 20,650 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,720 and a low of 20,600.
December rose 120 to 20,490, January 170 to 20,650, February 190 to 20,670, April 180 to 20,660, May 190 to 20,660 and June 110 to 20,620.
Combined volume fell to 53,370 tonnes from 81,670.
Copper opened higher and stayed around opening levels for most of the session. Traders said short-covering dominated today's trading but the future trend was not optimistic.
"Short-covering from retail investors pushed prices up but thin volume indicated a lack of confidence in the market," one trader said.
"Technical rebounds in the past two days did not pull copper out of its downward trend, which made most long position holders pessimistic," he added.
"Copper is preparing for falls and will drop whenever negative news emerges," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mostly up. December rose 50 to 13,850 yuan per tonne, January was unchanged at 14,050 and February rose 250 to 14,250.
Combined volume rose to 360 tonnes from 20.
